# [CS056] High Entropy String in Vendored Code (high-entropy-string)

Vendored dependency code contains a string that looks like a secret.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html) |
| **OWASP** | A07:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Long strings with high Shannon entropy in vendor/ are often embedded credentials or keys that were committed upstream or by a patch.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
// vendor/github.com/acme/client/config.go
const apiKey = "Zx9Lq2...44 random characters..."
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
// vendor/github.com/acme/client/config.go
apiKey := os.Getenv("ACME_API_KEY")
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [high-entropy-string]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    high-entropy-string: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore high-entropy-string -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** high-entropy-string
```
